Fixed additively. verify_inclusion_proof is now a public free function; the method stays and delegates.

The bead was right, and the crate own test suite proves it: pkix-ct/tests/merkle_inclusion.rs has an empty_verifier() helper whose doc comment reads "Empty verifier -- the verify_inclusion path uses neither the log list nor the SignatureVerifier (it is hash-only)". That is exactly the workaround the bead predicted -- "Build a phony SctVerifier::new(CtLogList::new(), some_verifier)" -- and the crate was already doing it to test its own function.

Change: the private verify_inclusion_inner became pub fn verify_inclusion_proof, documented and exported. Entirely additive -- no signature changed, nothing moved. SctVerifier::verify_inclusion remains and delegates to it, because the discoverability argument in its rustdoc is a real one (callers verifying SCTs are usually the ones who want inclusion proofs, and RFC 6962 2 groups the log-behaviour operations). Its docs now say which to prefer and why.

It also lands next to merkle_leaf_hash, merkle_tree_leaf_for_cert and merkle_tree_leaf_for_precert, which were already free functions for precisely the same reason -- computing a leaf hash needs no verifier either. So the inconsistency was that one hash-only operation out of four was method-only.

Scope correction to the bead title, which reads "verify_inclusion / verify_sth": verify_sth is NOT hash-only. It calls self.logs.get(log_id) and dispatches signature verification through self.verifier, so it belongs on the type and is untouched. Only verify_inclusion was misplaced.

Tests: every_leaf_verifies_without_a_verifier runs the free function over the same N7 and N11 fixtures as the existing every_leaf_verifies, so it is the identical check reached directly rather than a weaker one; and the_free_function_and_the_method_agree asserts they return the same result for both a good proof and a tampered root, so the delegation is one implementation and not two.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2360 tests.
